text:
Jen (AE): hey team — handing off a POC question from a financial customer. They want to avoid deploying an on‑prem proxy if possible. Questions: can we do PrivateLink + split‑tunnel (no proxy), provide stable egress IPs for their firewall, and what's the rough cost delta vs running a managed proxy? Also TLS inspect requirement is unclear. @Carlos can you advise on feasibility + firewall snippet?

Carlos (NetOps): quick clarifying q's: do they need client source IP preserved to the backend (i.e., origin IP on our side)? are they planning interface endpoints (PrivateLink) per-region or a single transit/NAT setup? any mTLS or mutual auth we need to terminate?

Jen (AE): they said they want allowlisting of a stable IP range (their firewall team is strict). they prefer minimal changes on their side — likely interface endpoints per VPC and split‑tunnel outbound. mTLS: TBD but could be mutual TLS to our ingress.

Priya (Solutions): recommended path (lowest ops): PrivateLink interface endpoint -> our PrivateDeploy/VPC endpoint (customer keeps split‑tunnel so traffic to us hits endpoint). Note: PrivateLink uplink will NAT to our egress EIP(s) (we provide the IPs), so we can give them an allowlist. Limitation: client source IP is not preserved through the endpoint NAT. If they need original client IP, we need a different topology (proxy or TCP passthrough + special routing).

Priya (Solutions): sample minimal firewall snippet we can give them (replace EIP with the ones we allocate):

```
ALLOW tcp 34.123.45.67/32 443 comment "Redwood PrivateLink endpoint egress"
ALLOW tcp 34.123.45.68/32 443 comment "Redwood failover egress"
```

Tom (EngInfra): cost/comms note: PrivateLink model: you pay for interface endpoints (per‑hour) + data processing per GB (cloud vendor), plus our Private deployment traffic if applicable. NAT/GW egress (if they NAT to Internet) has per‑GB cost too. Managed onprem proxy (our L7 edge) shifts some costs to instance/hour + data egress but gives you TLS termination options and preserves more control (and can support TLS inspect workflows). Ballpark: PrivateLink endpoint is cheap per hour (~$0.01/hr regionally) but data processing adds up — estimate +$0.02–0.08/GB depending on region. L7 proxy add-on is usually a fixed monthly/instance price in the POC quote (I can pull numbers for this account).

Carlos (NetOps): about TLS inspect: if the customer requires their firewall to inspect TLS between client and Redwood, PrivateLink alone won't help because TLS is end‑to‑end. For TLS inspect you either: 1) terminate TLS at their edge (so we see cleartext) — rare, or 2) proxy TLS at their side with a dedicated proxy that performs inspect and re‑establishes TLS to us, or 3) run an L7 proxy on our side and negotiate mTLS between parties. If the ask is "we need to see SNI for policy" — SNI will be visible unless they do something like ESNI/Encrypted SNI.

Carlos (NetOps): quick topology options (short):
- Option A (recommended low ops): Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) per VPC -> we advertise egress EIP(s) for allowlist. No client src IP preserved. Good for strict allowlist.
- Option B (client IP preserve need): TGW + routed setup or dedicated proxy in their VPC that preserves srcip via GRE/VXLAN -> more ops and firewall complexity.
- Option C (TLS inspect / advanced controls): L7 egress proxy (managed by customer or our managed proxy). More cost, supports TLS termination and SNI rewrite, preserves application visibility.

Tom (EngInfra): snippet for route/SG table to hand to platform team:

```
# route table on customer side for PrivateLink traffic
Destination: 10.0.0.0/8 -> InterfaceEndpointENI (accept PrivateLink traffic)
# security group on endpoint
Type: OUTBOUND TCP 443 -> 34.123.45.67/32
```

Priya (Solutions): action: I'll draft a 1‑page POC handoff with the three topology options, firewall snippet, and a rough cost comparison. I can include a sample AWS PrivateLink allowance CSV and suggest an allowlist template for their firewall. I'll also flag TLS inspect as an enterprise blocker for the simplest option.

Jen (AE): perfect. can you also include an ask for whether they need client IP in logs? that'll change the proposal. I'll schedule a 30m technical call tomorrow with their network/security folks and include the doc. :+1:

NetOps Bot: deployment-checker: note — no infra changes triggered. Reminder: when using PrivateLink we need to allocate egress EIPs and notify Security for allowlist issuance.

Carlos (NetOps): one more practical tip — if they insist on a single static IP block, plan for HA: provide 2–3 EIPs (active/passive) and document failover. We'll also recommend a short TTL DNS for any hostname endpoints in case we need to rotate IPs.

Tom (EngInfra): I'll assemble cost line items for proxy vs PrivateLink data processing and post in this thread before EOD.

Jen (AE): thanks everyone — will post meeting notes after call and attach Priya's handoff doc.
